answer: Each identity must answer a fresh challenge with a chain of sequential modular squarings; each step depends on the previous one, so GPUs cannot parallelize a single chain to reduce its elapsed time. A Wesolowski proof makes the result efficiently verifiable. Clones may run separate chains concurrently, but cannot make any one chain faster, imposing a per-identity time and compute cost—like crossing a canyon of steps, not changing its pigment or turning it into a dune.
